item.title: Lawrence Central High School gets new head football coach
item.description: Russ Mann has been hired as the new head football coach for Lawrence Central High School, replacing Will Patterson who joined Butler University's coaching staff earlier this year.

item.title: Colts’ Chris Ballard shares update on contract discussions with Daniel Jones
item.description: The Colts are in positive contract negotiations with quarterback Daniel Jones, who had an excellent 2025 season and is recovering from a torn Achilles, and are also hoping to bring back wide receiver Alec Pierce.

item.title: Indiana Michigan Power unveils customer benefits plan with rate reduction
item.description: Indiana Michigan Power (I&M) announced a Customer Benefits Plan that includes a rate reduction, a Benefits Bank to stabilize rates, and reliability improvements to reduce outages.

item.title: Marathon State of the Union touts Trump’s efforts; Dems ask if he’s helping America
item.description: In his State of the Union address, President Donald Trump touted his accomplishments while making false claims about voter fraud and tariffs, and blaming Democrats for high costs.

item.title: Indianapolis residents frustrated with potholes as Public Works ramps up repairs
item.description: The Department of Public Works in Indianapolis has patched over 46,000 potholes since Jan. 1 and has increased its budget by $10 million to speed up repairs and prevent further damage.

item.title: Senate advances Indianapolis school corporation bill
item.description: The Senate narrowly approved a bill to create the Indianapolis Public Education Corporation, which would consist of nine members appointed by the mayor of Indianapolis and have authority over IPS' budget, while the elected IPS board would retain control of day-to-day operations.

item.title: Stricter immigration enforcement in Indiana nears final vote
item.description: Senate Bill 76, also known as the "Fairness Act", has passed both chambers of the Indiana General Assembly and would require schools, police, and local governments to cooperate with Federal Immigration Officials, while also allowing the state's Attorney General to take action on businesses that knowingly hire undocumented workers.

item.title: Indiana schools eye the potential impact of state’s sweeping immigration bill
item.description: Indiana's SB 76 bill could affect K-12 schools by requiring greater cooperation between local governments and federal immigration authorities, potentially leading to increased fear of immigration enforcement and greater absenteeism.

item.title: Johnson County teen pleads guilty to rape and strangulation of 79-year-old woman
item.description: Ariahn Smith, who was 16 at the time, pleaded guilty to rape and strangulation of a 79-year-old woman in October and is being held in Johnson County Jail awaiting sentencing on March 12.
